section_summary: This section consists chiefly of inquiries from American holders of Japanese bonds and State Department replies explaining the uncertain prospects for payment after the war. It also contains correspondence about Taiwan Electric Power Company bonds, including a request for information from the American consulate in Taipei. The final exchange concerns Tokyo Electric Company bonds and the shortage of foreign exchange in Japan.

subfiles.title: Reply recording Louise Hartford’s Yokohama bond
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges information about Hartford’s City of Yokohama bond.
subfiles.summary: The Department records her bond information for possible future use.

subfiles.title: E. F. Burdick’s inquiry about a Tokyo bond
subfiles.about: Burdick asks about interest and sinking fund payments on a City of Tokyo bond.
subfiles.summary: Burdick asks what happened to payments on his bond.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to E. F. Burdick
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains its policy on defaulted Japanese municipal bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department cannot predict settlement terms and generally does not negotiate directly for bondholders. It recommends the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council and offers to record Burdick’s holdings and citizenship details.

subfiles.title: I. E. Enlow’s inquiry about an Oriental Development bond
subfiles.about: Enlow requests the status and value of a Japanese guaranteed bond.
subfiles.summary: Enlow asks about his bond and funds deposited in New York for bond payments.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to I. E. Enlow
subfiles.from: Gardner E. Palmer, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department discusses possible recovery on Enlow’s bond and blocked debt service funds.
subfiles.summary: The Department cannot predict the bond’s value or future claims treatment. It recommends the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council and directs Enlow to the Office of Alien Property for information about blocked payment funds.

subfiles.title: Instructions to the American consulate in Taipei
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Taipei
subfiles.about: The Department requests information about Taiwan Electric Power Company and its outstanding dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: The consulate is asked to investigate ownership, debt service, outstanding bonds and prospects for payment.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to James Grafton Rogers
subfiles.about: The Department acknowledges the Council’s proposal concerning Taiwan Electric Power Company bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department says it is considering the proposal and will respond.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Leroy C. Hickey
subfiles.from: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains its policy toward Hickey’s Japanese government bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Department cannot predict peace treaty provisions or repayment. It recommends the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council and offers to record details of Hickey’s purchase and American citizenship.

subfiles.title: Treasury referral of Hickey’s inquiry
subfiles.to: James C. Corliss, Department of State
subfiles.about: Treasury forwards Hickey’s inquiry for a response.
subfiles.summary: Treasury forwards Hickey’s letter and its acknowledgment.

subfiles.title: Treasury acknowledgment to Hickey
subfiles.about: Treasury acknowledges Hickey’s bond inquiry and refers it to State.
subfiles.summary: Treasury refers the inquiry to the Department of State.

subfiles.title: Leroy C. Hickey’s inquiry about two Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: Hickey asks whether his bonds retain value and whether interest or principal will be paid.
subfiles.summary: Hickey reports no interest payments since May 1942 and requests guidance.

subfiles.title: Council petition concerning Taiwan Electric Power Company bonds
subfiles.from: James Grafton Rogers, Foreign Bondholders Protective Council
subfiles.about: The Council urges renewed service on Taiwan Electric Power Company dollar bonds.
subfiles.summary: The Council describes the company’s bond issue, wartime interruption of service and estimated dollar bonds still held outside Japan. Citing a possible American loan to improve the plant, it asks the government to press for payment of arrears and renewed debt service.

subfiles.title: Bondholder’s citizenship information
subfiles.about: A correspondent supplies birth details requested for a bondholding record.
subfiles.summary: The writer reports birth in Los Angeles on February 21, 1915.

subfiles.title: E. C. Gathings forwards Leo J. Mundt’s inquiry
subfiles.to: E. W. Doherty, Department of State
subfiles.about: Gathings asks whether provision will be made for Mundt’s Japanese government bonds.
subfiles.summary: Gathings forwards Mundt’s letter and requests advice.

subfiles.title: Leo J. Mundt’s inquiry about Japanese bonds
subfiles.about: Mundt seeks a route to recovery on his prewar Japanese government bonds.
subfiles.summary: Mundt asks about payment prospects and possible distribution of vested Japanese property to American creditors.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to E. C. Gathings
subfiles.from: Ernest A. Gross, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department addresses Mundt’s possible claim against vested Japanese assets.
subfiles.summary: The Department says the filing deadline for claims under the Trading with the Enemy Act has passed. Claims exceed vested Japanese assets, so substantial recovery depends on a future resumption of debt service; it suggests contacting the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.

subfiles.title: Congressional inquiry for R. B. Carlisle
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Satterthwaite, Department of State
subfiles.about: Rees asks how Carlisle can protect his City of Yokohama bond investment.
subfiles.summary: Rees reports Carlisle missed a claims filing deadline and seeks advice.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Edward L. Rees
subfiles.from: Ernest A. Gross, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains Carlisle’s missed claims deadline and uncertain bond recovery.
subfiles.summary: The Department says Carlisle’s claim against vested assets appears barred if he did not file in time. It expects only nominal distributions even for timely claims, sees no near term debt service negotiations and recommends the Foreign Bondholders Protective Council.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Burt D. Pearson
subfiles.from: Gardner E. Palmer, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department addresses Pearson’s question about registering his Japanese government bonds.
subfiles.summary: No filing with State is required, though it will record Pearson’s holdings. The deadline for claims against vested assets has passed; recovery from those assets is expected to be negligible, and future value may depend on Japanese debt service after a peace settlement.

subfiles.title: Burt D. Pearson’s bond filing inquiry
subfiles.about: Pearson asks whether he must file details of two Japanese government bonds.
subfiles.summary: Pearson describes his bonds and requests filing instructions.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to E. A. Seamands
subfiles.from: Gardner E. Palmer, Department of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains the lack of a payment procedure for Mrs. Seamands’s bond.
subfiles.summary: The Department cites Japan’s shortage of foreign exchange, uncertain claims legislation and the possibility of future Japanese debt service.

subfiles.title: Consular transmittal of Seamands reply
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Bombay
subfiles.about: The Department sends its reply for possible delivery to Seamands.
subfiles.summary: The consulate may forward the enclosed letter.

subfiles.title: E. A. Seamands’s claim inquiry
subfiles.about: Seamands asks how his wife can obtain payment on her Japanese government bond.
subfiles.summary: Seamands describes Mrs. Seamands’s $1,000 bond and requests a claims procedure.

subfiles.title: Draft consular transmittal of Seamands reply
subfiles.to: American Consular Officer in Charge, Bombay
subfiles.about: A second version authorizes forwarding the Seamands reply.
subfiles.summary: The consulate may transmit the enclosed letter to Seamands.

subfiles.title: Raymond T. Jackson’s inquiry about Tokyo Electric bonds
subfiles.about: Jackson asks about renewed payments on Tokyo Electric Company bonds and criticizes government policy toward foreign investments.
subfiles.summary: Jackson renews an earlier inquiry about interest and principal payments. He argues that postwar treatment of private property and foreign bondholders undermines confidence in American investment abroad.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Raymond T. Jackson
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Financial Affairs
subfiles.about: The Department explains why Tokyo Electric bond payments cannot currently resume.
subfiles.summary: The Department says American bondholders’ rights have not been surrendered. Japan lacks foreign exchange for interest or principal payments, and available exchange is reserved for essential imports; the Department promises support when Japan can again meet international obligations.
